passageTitle: Passage 1 — The history of urban parks
passageText:
In the nineteenth century, cities in Europe and North America grew very quickly. Many people moved from the countryside to work in factories. Cities became crowded and dirty, and most people had little green space near their homes. Doctors at the time believed that fresh air and walking in nature were good for people's health, so city leaders began to think about building public parks.

One of the first parks of this kind was Birkenhead Park in England, which opened in 1847. It was the first park in the world paid for with public money, so everyone could visit it for free. The park had lakes, trees, and long paths for walking. It became very popular, and it gave ideas to park designers in other countries.

In the United States, the most famous example is Central Park in New York. It was designed in 1858 by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux, who had visited Birkenhead Park. They wanted to create a quiet, green place in the middle of a busy city. The park has large open lawns, a lake for boating, and many trees. It is still one of the most visited parks in the world today.

Early parks were not built mainly for sport. Their main purpose was to give people fresh air, a place to walk, and a break from busy city life. Later, in the twentieth century, parks began to add playgrounds, sports fields, and swimming pools, so they became places for active fun as well as for rest.

Today, urban parks have many uses. They help to cool cities in summer, give homes to birds and insects, and provide a place for markets, concerts, and community events. Many people also use them to exercise and to meet friends. At weekends, families often meet in parks for picnics, games, and quiet walks under the trees, and children play safely far from busy roads. However, many parks now face problems with money, because local governments often have to cut their budgets. Without enough care, trees die and paths become broken. Many cities are now looking for new ways to protect their parks for the future.
